newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain hails Mexico's expulsion of ETA suspect.
newsitem.headline: Spain hails Mexico's expulsion of ETA suspect.

text.p: Spain wecomed Mexico's expulsion and transfer to Spain of accused ETA Basque separatist rebel Pedro Maria Garmendia on Friday, saying it was indicative of a positive policy change.

"It shows a very significant change in the attitude of the Mexican authorities with respect to their policy on expulsions and extraditions of ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) members," the Interior Ministry said in a statement.

Garmendia arrived in Madrid's Barajas airport on a regular flight at about 1500 GMT. Mexican authorities handed him over to Spanish National Police at the airport and then the High Court ordered him to prison, the statement said.
He arrived in Mexico in 1989 after serving seven years of a 10-year sentence in France for a robbery in Andorra.

Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar met Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo in September and requested the expulsion of Garmendia, wanted for arms possession and ETA activities, along with two other alleged ETA members seeking refuge in Mexico.
Aznar pledged to help Mexico fight against a new guerrilla group -- the Popular Revolutionary Army -- that has called for the overthrow of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Pary.
ETA has killed some 800 people since 1968 when the group started a separatist drive for the Basque region.
